test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Moplah Uprising, an organised opposition of Muslim cultivators, occurred in which modern state of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Moplah Uprising, also known as the Mappila Rebellion, occurred in the Malabar region of Kerala in 1921.
 
• This rebellion was led by the Mappila Muslims of Kerala, who were primarily tenants and cultivators.
 
• The uprising was a reaction against British colonial rule and the oppressive practices of landlords.
 
• The rebellion saw widespread violence and was one of the significant peasant movements in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• It was part of the larger Khilafat Movement and Non-Cooperation Movement against British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilafat Movement:**

 
 
• A pan-Islamist political campaign launched by Muslims in British India to influence the British government not to abolish the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• It was led by prominent Muslim leaders like Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, this was a mass protest against British rule.
 
• It aimed at inducing the British government to grant self-governance to India.
 
 
 
• **Malabar Region:**
 
 
• Located in the northern part of Kerala, the Malabar region was historically significant due to its trading ports.
 
• It was a major center for the spice trade and saw various foreign influences over centuries.
 
 
 
• **Tenant Farming:**
 
 
• A system where farmers cultivate land owned by another and pay rent in the form of cash or a portion of the produce.
 
• In the Malabar region, the oppressive practices by landlords led to widespread discontent among tenant farmers.
